source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Use temperature readings to compare which body is hotter or colder.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The 50°F body is hotter than the 20°C body.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: The 20°C body is hotter than the 40°C body.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: The red body is hotter than the blue body, even though both are 30°C.

intelligence.enrichment: A hotter body has a higher temperature than a colder body, and the difference in temperature tells how hot one body is compared with another. As the temperature reading increases on the same scale, the body is judged hotter; as it decreases, the body is judged colder. The learner correctly applies this rule: A hotter body has a higher temperature than a colder body, and the difference in temperature tells how hot one body is compared with another. A temperature number is just a label, so a body at 25 °C could be hotter than a body at 40 °C if it feels hotter.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 6 Science question. Chapter: Temperature and its measurement. The student must decide: Use temperature readings to compare which body is hotter or colder. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE. If the stem numbers activities 1..n, every number must appear in an option (or in a structured part's first-class options). Two-tier (choose, then reason) is welcome: put A/B/C on part.options, not typed into part text.
